name: Coda

field_reviews.reason: Live developer docs (coda.io/developers, now branded Superhuman Docs API) confirm auth is an API token from the account page passed as 'Authorization: Bearer <api_token>'; every endpoint lists Bearer authorization.
API token over Bearer header is the only documented REST API auth. (The MCP server additionally supports OAuth 2 with PKCE, which the draft correctly kept in mcp_notes rather than auth_methods.)
Developer docs state verbatim that the API is 'available to all of our users free of charge, in both free and paid workspaces', with tokens generated self-serve from account settings.

API reference covers docs, pages, tables, rows, columns, controls, folders, permissions, Packs and analytics but not org-level admin; 'medium' is a fair rating. Composio's CODA toolkit wraps 110 tools within this surface.
RESTful API at coda.io/apis/v1 confirmed; hosted vendor MCP servers confirmed at coda.io/apis/mcp and docs.superhuman.com/apis/mcp.

High-risk vendor-ownership claim verified: the Superhuman help center security article states 'The Superhuman Docs MCP server is officially published at https://docs.superhuman.com/apis/mcp' and that the earlier Coda MCP at coda.io/apis/mcp 'is still officially supported'. Both endpoints are on vendor-owned domains (coda.io / superhuman.com after the rebrand), not community repos. Composio CODA toolkit page confirms API_KEY auth, 110 tools, 4 triggers.
Free self-serve API tokens, documented REST API and an official hosted MCP server; buildable today.
No blocker: signup, tokens and API access are free and self-serve.

notes: Focus was the high-risk official-vendor-MCP claim: confirmed via the Superhuman help center (help.superhuman.com security article naming docs.superhuman.com/apis/mcp as the officially published endpoint and coda.io/apis/mcp as still officially supported) and independent coverage noting the official hosted server went public beta April 2026, distinct from older community servers. help.superhuman.com sits behind a Cloudflare bot wall on direct fetch but content was verifiable via search indexing. Also re-opened coda.io/developers (free-of-charge statement, Bearer auth, inbound-only 'trigger automation' webhook endpoint consistent with supports_webhooks=false) and the Composio CODA toolkit (110 tools, 4 triggers, API_KEY). The Coda-to-Superhuman-Docs rebrand described in the draft is real and correctly handled.
